text:
Jordan: Heads up — product asked whether we can keep full OTEL spans for 90 days for debugging, but we also need to meet compliance for PII. thoughts?
Amira: Do we have a concrete list of PII fields in spans right now? email, user_id, payment refs?
Ravi: Mostly email, user_id (internal), ip_address, and occasionally request body in error traces.
Sasha: TL;DR: we shouldn't keep raw PII in long-term storage. Options: redact at collector, pseudonymize (hash + salt) + reversible KMS-encrypted mapping for audits, or keep raw for short window then purge.
Jordan: Product wants searchable traces for incidents. Hashing breaks human-readable search.
Amira: We can keep searchable tokens via reversible tokenization: store token in trace index, mapping in HSM-backed store with strict audit logs. KMS unwrap only for authorized IR runbooks.
Ravi: Implementation tradeoffs: collector-side processors add CPU/latency. If we do it in exporter (near storage) we preserve pipeline speed but risk raw data existing in internal transport.
Sasha: Agree. Also need to consider exporters that send to third-party analytics. Those need to only receive sanitized data.
telemetry-bot: Reminder: current telemetry retention policy (RFC-41) is 30d for spans by default. Any change requires compliance signoff.
Jordan: For audits we need an append-only access log tied to an approval flow. Security, are there existing authz hooks we can call? @Amira can you loop them in?
Amira: Yup, I'll ping sec. My proposal: collector has a PII processor pipeline: attribute allowlist -> pseudonymize selected attrs with salted HMAC -> send traces to hot index (30d full) + cold index (90d pseudonymized). For audits, authorized requests can call a service to rehydrate specific trace(s) by fetching encrypted mapping from KMS with operator approval.
Ravi: That sounds okay. Can we sketch the OTEL processor config? Something like:
```yaml
processors:
  pii_removal:
    deny_fields: ["http.request.body", "user.email", "user.ip"]
    pseudonymize:
      fields: ["user.id", "session.id"]
      salt: /etc/telemetry/salt
exporters:
  redacted_storage:
    endpoint: https://redacted-storage.internal
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      processors: [pii_removal]
      exporters: [redacted_storage]
```
Sasha: Need to ensure salt is rotated and stored in vault. HMAC vs AES? HMAC gives consistent non-reversible tokens; AES deterministic encryption allows reversible but needs strict KMS policies.
Amira: Use AES-GCM with KMS-wrapped DEKs for reversible mapping, and also keep HMAC tokens for quick lookups in the index. Dual store approach.
Jordan: Two quick asks: 1) can we avoid changing exporters used by customers (hosted API)? 2) How do we prove compliance for audits?
Ravi: (1) For hosted API we can perform sanitization in our private collector before it hits customer-visible exporters. That keeps customer pipelines intact. (2) For audits, we provide an audit trail: who requested unwrap, what trace ids, justification, timestamps. Add immutable log entry to SIEM.
Sasha: Also perf note: deterministic encryption lookups require an index on token; need to benchmark storage cost.
Amira: I'll draft an RFC with: threat model, latency budget impact, OTEL processor config, KMS key rotation plan, audit flow, and a migration plan (30d->90d windows split).
Jordan: Great. Security wants a short-run proof-of-concept before rollout — can we do a canary for one service?
Ravi: Yep. I'll wire up a collector config for payments-staging and run it for two weeks.
telemetry-bot: New action created: RFC-telemetry-pii-tokenization (assigned: Amira)
Jordan: Thanks folks. tagging follow-ups: @Sasha please add index perf estimates; @Ravi please attach collector config and perf numbers to RFC; @Amira loop in security/compliance. :thumbsup:
